author: mentor (Claude, 27 Oct 2026), for the organisation's agents to read at decision time; never training data
note: Each lesson says when it applies and how it is checked. 'test' names a check that mentor.py runs on our own daily data, so the lesson carries current numbers; lessons without one are experience, labelled as unverified until a test exists. Agents may use lessons as background, never as evidence to cite.

lessons.title: Four of our eight shares are banks
lessons.lesson: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and SBI move together: an RBI surprise, a credit scare or foreign selling hits all four at once. Three banks in a top-3 portfolio is closer to one bet than three.

lessons.title: ITC and NTPC usually fall less than the banks
lessons.lesson: ITC (consumer staples) and NTPC (a regulated utility) tend to move less than the market; in a sell-off they often hold up better, and in a strong rally they often lag. Their low beta is a risk trait, not a forecast.

lessons.title: Momentum can fail sharply when a fall turns into a rebound
lessons.lesson: After a crash, the shares that fell most often rebound most, so a momentum rule holding the past winners can lag badly in the rebound months. Be cautious about momentum entries right after a deep market fall.

lessons.title: Trading costs decide small edges
lessons.lesson: Each rebalance pays brokerage, STT, charges and slippage (about 0.15% one way in our model). A strategy that trades monthly needs a real edge of several tenths of a percent a month just to stand still against holding the basket.

lessons.title: Results days carry gap risk
lessons.lesson: A share can jump or fall several percent on its quarterly results, regardless of its trend. A position opened a few days before results carries that event risk in addition to the signal; check the events calendar.

lessons.title: RBI and Fed decision days move rate-sensitive shares
lessons.lesson: Banks react most to RBI policy surprises, and the rupee and foreign flows react to the US Federal Reserve. A move just before a policy decision is often positioning, not a new trend.

lessons.title: Infosys earns in dollars
lessons.lesson: Most of Infosys' revenue is in foreign currency: a weaker rupee tends to help its margins, and US technology spending and US interest rates matter more to it than Indian demand.

lessons.title: Reliance is oil, retail and telecom at once
lessons.lesson: Reliance's earnings mix refining and petrochemicals (oil prices and margins), retail and Jio (telecom); news about one business, such as a listing of a unit, can move the share even when the others are unchanged.

lessons.title: An ex-dividend drop is not a loss
lessons.lesson: On the ex-date the price falls by about the dividend, which the holder receives; our scoring restates dividends, so judge the total return, never the price drop alone.

lessons.title: After SEVERE distribution days, falls are deeper
lessons.lesson: On our history, the 20 sessions after a SEVERE regime saw deeper average worst falls than after NORMAL days. It warns about risk; it did not time profitable exits, so size cautiously rather than sell everything.

lessons.title: The best backtest of the past rarely stays best
lessons.lesson: Choosing each year the idea with the best record over the previous years lost to the basket on our history. Trust live, pre-registered results over any backtest, including your own reasoning about why something worked.
